To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the tri-bimaximally-mixed neutrino mixing matrix can be corrected by the non-unitary effects from charged lepton sector, (ii) the non-unitary corrections can lead to a non-zero value for the mixing angle theta(13), (iii) the non-unitarity effects are constrained by current experimental data, and (iv) the non-unitarities are model-dependent, which can be used as a test of flavor symmetry models.

(i) the non-unitarity of the 3 x3 neutrino mixing is a generic property of A(4) flavor models; (ii) the non-unitary corrections can be large and lead to a sizable deviation from the tri-bimaxmal mixing; and (iii) the current experimental constraints allow us to constrain some model parameters to some extend.
In a class of A4 flavor models, small corrections to the tri-bimaxial neutrino mixing pattern can be generated, and these corrections can result in a non-unitary 3 x 4 mixing matrix.
